description:
Finding: imap/src/config.rs AuthConfig::is_dev_mode() checks 3 conditions: !required && users.is_empty() && credential_file.is_none(). reader/src/config.rs AuthConfig::is_dev_mode() checks 6 conditions: also oidc_providers.is_empty() && client_certs.is_empty() && trusted_issuers.is_empty(). The imap AuthConfig struct omits those fields (correctly, imap doesn't support OIDC or client certs), but there is no comment in imap/src/config.rs stating that imap's is_dev_mode() intentionally has a reduced condition set compared to the reader's version.

Risk: If a future maintainer adds OIDC support to imap (plausible — the credential_store build call on main.rs line 161 already uses stoa_auth::build_credential_store), they will add an oidc_providers field to imap's AuthConfig but may not notice that is_dev_mode() also needs updating. An imap with OIDC configured but no local users would incorrectly return is_dev_mode() = true and fail the startup guard, blocking a valid production configuration. The lack of any comment pointing to reader's version makes this a silent trap.

Suggested fix: Add a comment above imap's is_dev_mode() documenting why it checks fewer conditions than reader's, and which conditions would need adding if auth features expand. Example: '// Intentionally simpler than reader AuthConfig::is_dev_mode() — imap does not support // OIDC, client certs, or trusted issuers. If those are added, update this method.'
title: imap AuthConfig::is_dev_mode() can silently diverge from reader's
